identity.name: Batavian Republic
alt_names: Batavian Republic and Kingdom of Holland

land.text: the Netherlands of the old Dutch Republic, less what the Treaty of The Hague took in May 1795

predecessors.note: 'It was proclaimed on 19 January 1795 after the Batavian Revolution'; infobox predecessor Dutch Republic. The dutch-republic dossier ends in January 1795. Cliopatria's Dutch Republic shape (980 cells) carries the VOC colonies.

land.text: the Kingdom of Holland, abolished 'by Imperial Decree' and incorporated into the French Empire on 9 July 1810

successors.note: Infobox 'Annexed by France: 9 July 1810'. The Batavian page names the Kingdom of Holland (5 June 1806) as the republic's successor; this dossier keeps both because Cliopatria's single row runs 1796-1810.

capitals.name: The Hague
capitals.note: Batavian infobox 'Capital: The Hague'; Kingdom page 'The Hague (1806-1808)'. Amsterdam is the largest city.

rulers.name: Rutger Jan Schimmelpenninck (Grand Pensionary / Raadpensionaris)
rulers.title: Grand Pensionary
rulers.note: 'On 10 May 1805, Schimmelpenninck was therefore inaugurated as Raadpensionaris'; the republic ended on 5 June 1806. The executive before 1805 (directories, Staatsbewind) is not listed on the pages opened.

rulers.name: Louis Bonaparte (King of Holland)
rulers.title: king
rulers.note: 'installed as King of Holland on 5 June 1806'; 'abdicated on 1 July in favour of his son'.

rulers.name: Son of Louis Bonaparte (named in the abdication)
rulers.title: king
rulers.note: The Batavian page: the son 'reigned for ten days' after the abdication; Louis 'abdicated on 2 July 1810' there, '1 July' on the Kingdom page. Not named on the pages opened.

correction.text: the Netherlands of the Batavian Republic of 1803 plus the lands the Treaty of The Hague took on 16 May 1795

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1795: Cliopatria's first shape begins in 1796, but the republic was 'proclaimed on 19 January 1795'. From 19 January to 16 May 1795 the republic holds the old Dutch Republic's territory; the Treaty of The Hague then takes 'Maastricht, Venlo, and Zeelandic Flanders' (ledger). The shape of 1803 is the nearest Cliopatria extent (without the colonies).

correction.text: the Netherlands of the republic (the 1803 extent), without Maastricht, Venlo and Zeelandic Flanders, ceded on 16 May 1795; the colonies are drawn by dutch-east-india-company and dutch-east-indies

keyframe_review.note: 259,681 km2 for 1796-1802 spreading from the Netherlands (3.4E) to Indonesia (134.7E, -10.4N): the colonies of the Dutch East India Company, which was Batavian only from 1799 ('the Asiatic Council replaced the VOC's Directorate in 1799') and whose possessions the dutch-east-india-company and dutch-east-indies dossiers draw (the VOC to 31 December 1799, the Indies from 1800). The page gives no area. The European part is the 1803 shape, without Maastricht, Venlo and Zeelandic Flanders, ceded on 16 May 1795.

35,837 km2 for 1803-1806: the Netherlands north of the Meuse without the lands of 1795. The page has no area (the Batavian infobox gives population 1,883,009 in 1795, 2,178,000 in 1806). The colonies returned by the Treaty of Amiens, 'soon recaptured by the British' after 1803, are in the colony dossiers (dutch-cape-colony, dutch-east-indies).

39,337 km2 for 1807-1808: the 1803 shape plus 11 cells at the German frontier, 9 of them inside Prussia's 1806 shape, which fits 'In 1807, the adjacent German regions of East Frisia and Jever were added to the kingdom'. The page's 'with the exception of the province of Limburg, and parts of Zeeland' agrees with the shape.

The same 39,337 km2 for 1809-1810. In 1810 Holland 'had to surrender all territories south of the River Rhine to France' (treaty of March 1810) and was annexed on 9 July 1810; the shape does not show the March loss (Zeeland and Brabant), which the ledger takes off. Area per page: none.

region.text: the Netherlands of the old Dutch Republic, which fell to the French and the Batavian revolutionaries in January 1795

ledger.note: 19 January 1795: the Batavian Republic is proclaimed. 'It was proclaimed on 19 January 1795 after the Batavian Revolution'; infobox 'transfer of power 18-19 January 1795', capital The Hague, 'Sister republic of the French First Republic'. The page names no frontier; the Netherlands of the Dutch Republic is the researcher's reading.

16 May 1795: the Treaty of The Hague cuts Maastricht, Venlo and Zeelandic Flanders away. The Batavian Republic 'ceded to France the territories of Maastricht, Venlo, and Zeelandic Flanders'; the treaty 'was signed on May 16, 1795' with a 100 million guilder indemnity and 25,000 French occupying troops. The Batavian page: 'a harsh Treaty of The Hague was concluded on 16 May 1795'.

October 1801: the Batavian Republic becomes the Batavian Commonwealth (Bataafs Gemenebest). 'From October 1801, the state was known as the Batavian Commonwealth'; the 1801 constitution 'expanded executive power', the executive being the Staatsbewind.
10 May 1805: Schimmelpenninck becomes Grand Pensionary. 'On 10 May 1805, Schimmelpenninck was therefore inaugurated as Raadpensionaris'; the colour and the state continue.

5 June 1806: Louis Bonaparte becomes King of Holland and the republic becomes the Kingdom of Holland. 'Louis Bonaparte was installed as King of Holland on 5 June 1806'; the Batavian infobox 'Kingdom of Holland 5 June 1806'; Louis entered The Hague on 23 June 1806. The Batavian page names the kingdom its successor; kept in this dossier because Cliopatria's row runs to 1810.

region.text: the adjacent German regions of East Frisia and Jever (the difference between Cliopatria's 1807 and 1803 shapes)

ledger.note: 1807: East Frisia and Jever are added to the Kingdom of Holland. 'In 1807, the adjacent German regions of East Frisia and Jever were added to the kingdom.' The page does not say who held them: East Frisia is inside Cliopatria's Prussia shape of 1806 and Prussia is the counterpart on that reading (Jever's previous holder is not on the page). Cliopatria's shape grows by 11 cells in 1807.
1808: the capital moves from The Hague to Utrecht, and in the same year to Amsterdam. The Kingdom infobox lists 'The Hague (1806-1808); Utrecht (1808); Amsterdam (1808-1810)'; months are not given.

region.text: all territories south of the River Rhine, ceded to France by the treaty of March 1810

ledger.note: March 1810: Holland surrenders the lands south of the Rhine to France. 'had to surrender all territories south of the River Rhine to France' after the Walcheren campaign, by 'the treaty of March 1810'; the page also speaks of the lands 'between the Meuse and the Scheldt' without reconciling the two. Zeeland and North Brabant are the researcher's reading of 'south of the Rhine'; Limburg and part of Zeeland were not Dutch already.

region.text: the Kingdom of Holland, incorporated into the French Empire

ledger.note: 9 July 1810: the Kingdom of Holland is annexed to the French Empire. 'Louis Bonaparte abdicated on 1 July in favour of his son'; 'On 4 July, French troops captured Amsterdam'; 'By Imperial Decree the Kingdom of Holland was abolished and incorporated into the French Empire'; infobox 'Annexed by France: 9 July 1810' (Batavian page: Louis abdicated on 2 July and the decree of 9 July; territorial-evolution page 'The Kingdom of Holland (1810)').

wars.name: Franco-Dutch campaign of the winter of 1794-1795
wars.outcome: 'After seizing the Low Countries in a surprise winter attack, France established the Batavian Republic as a puppet state'; Pichegru invaded in January 1795; the Treaty of The Hague (16 May 1795) took Maastricht, Venlo and Zeelandic Flanders.
wars.note: The French occupation of 1795 also fixed a French army of 25,000 at Dutch expense (secret clause).

wars.name: Walcheren campaign and the end of the Kingdom of Holland

zones.text: the territories south of the Rhine

wars.outcome: Holland 'had to surrender all territories south of the River Rhine to France' after the Walcheren campaign; Louis abdicated on 1 July 1810 and the kingdom was annexed on 9 July 1810.
wars.note: Britain is named by the page only as the Walcheren expedition's side; not a state described there.

certainty.note: The Netherlands' frontiers are the old Dutch Republic's, fixed by the Treaty of The Hague (16 May 1795) and the 1807 and 1810 changes; the East Frisian border of 1807 and the Rhine line of 1810 are the page's wording, not a surveyed line.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Batavian Republic' 1796..1810 (four shapes): the 1796-1802 shape includes Indonesia and is replaced by the 1803 shape (colonies are in dutch-east-india-company and dutch-east-indies); the 1807-1810 shapes are the Kingdom of Holland (Louis Bonaparte, 5 June 1806 to 9 July 1810), kept here because Cliopatria has no separate row; the Batavian page itself says the republic ended on 5 June 1806 and names the Kingdom of Holland as successor, so a split into batavian-republic (1795-1806) and kingdom-of-holland (1806-1810) is a legitimate alternative (a gap-filler can split it). Cliopatria's 1796 shape has no 1795 predecessor: a new keyframe 1795 is added. The state began on 19 January 1795 (page) and Cliopatria begins in 1796. Page silent / not settled within the 5-page budget (3 opened): the Dutch colonies seized by Britain 1795-1806 (Cape, Ceylon, Guiana) and returned by the Treaty of Amiens, whose date the Batavian page does not give; the 1798 coups and constitutions (not territorial); the Treaty of Fontainebleau/Tilsit that gave East Frisia and Jever (the Kingdom page does not name it); the precise lands south of the Rhine in 1810 (the page contradicts itself, 'south of the Rhine' against 'between the Meuse and the Scheldt'); the 1810 date of the treaty (only 'March 1810'). Gazetteer names needed: place 'Venlo', region 'Zeelandic Flanders' (Zeeuws-Vlaanderen). The French First Republic dossier lists the Batavian Republic as a vassal (sister republic) from 1795; the French Directory continues it. Dates differ between pages: Louis abdicated on 1 July (Kingdom page) or 2 July (Batavian page) 1810; the annexation is 9 July on both.
